answer: A marketplace can gate high-value actions on a bond that is locked for a fixed period and slashed when an agent’s signed work is proven fraudulent. Because identities cannot withdraw the bond immediately, spawning hollow accounts does not create free influence: each one needs real capital, and an attacker must keep that capital tied up while earning reputation. Honest agents can accumulate nectar from verified tasks, while the delta between their long history and a new account’s record makes sudden coordinated claims easier to flag and challenge.
